sections.heading: Why brownfields win the power race
bullets: The scarce asset in AI buildout isn't land or GPUs — it's an energized grid connection; new interconnection requests can queue for 5+ years

A retired coal plant or aluminum smelter already has the substation, the high-voltage lines, and the utility relationship — a data center can plug into decades-old infrastructure in a fraction of the time
TeraWulf's whole platform is this play: Lake Mariner on a former 700 MW coal plant, its Kentucky campus on a smelter that drew ~480 MW continuously, plus two more coal-legacy sites
An aluminum smelter is the perfect donor: it consumed steady, massive power 24/7 — exactly the load profile a data center brings back

sections.heading: Gross MW vs critical IT MW
bullets: Gross (or facility) MW is everything the site draws from the grid; critical IT MW is what actually reaches the computers — the difference is cooling, power conversion losses, and building overhead
PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness) is the ratio: a PUE of 1.25 means 1.25 MW drawn per 1 MW of IT load — modern liquid-cooled builds target 1.2-1.3 vs ~1.5+ for older air-cooled facilities
Leases and build costs are quoted per critical-IT MW (~$9-12M per MW to build) because that's the unit tenants pay for

Converting a bitcoin-mining hall to AI hosting is a rebuild, not a retrofit: mining runs cheap air-cooled racks at ~30 kW with no redundancy; AI tenants need direct-to-chip liquid cooling at 130+ kW per rack, backup power, and Tier III-style concurrent maintainability

sections.heading: How a thin-credit tenant signs a $6.7B lease: credit enhancement
bullets: The problem: AI-cloud middlemen (like Fluidstack) want gigawatts but have small balance sheets — no lender will fund a $1B+ building against their promise alone
The fix: a third party with an investment-grade balance sheet 'backstops' the lease — guaranteeing payments (up to a cap) if the tenant defaults, sometimes agreeing to assume the lease outright

The backstopper gets paid in upside: penny warrants (rights to buy shares for ~$0.01) — insurance premium paid in equity; at TeraWulf, Google's ~$4.5B of backstops earned warrants worth ~14% of the company
Backstops typically amortize (shrink) as the project proves out, and carry escape triggers — the landlord keeps residual risk beyond the guarantee
Once the lease is credit-enhanced, project-level debt can fund construction: bonds secured by the lease payments themselves, issued by a subsidiary that owns just that project

sections.heading: Reading a landlord's P&L without being fooled
bullets: Warrants held by outsiders are a liability that gets re-measured every quarter: when the stock price RISES, the warrants become more valuable, and the company books a LOSS (and vice versa) — pure accounting, zero cash

This makes GAAP earnings anti-correlated with success: a landlord whose stock doubles on new leases will print enormous 'losses' from warrant marks — TeraWulf booked a $755.7M warrant charge in one quarter and the stock barely moved
The metrics that matter instead: contracted MW, energization schedule vs plan, $/MW build cost vs guidance, NOI margin per lease, and cash on hand vs remaining capex
Take-or-pay backlog converts to revenue only when buildings energize — the gap between 'contracted' and 'billing' MW is the execution risk, measured in transformer and switchgear lead times

sections.heading: The tenant chain: who's really paying the rent
bullets: AI capacity often arrives through layers: a frontier lab rents from a cloud middleman, who leases from a landlord, whose lender relies on a backstopper — four balance sheets in one building
Following the chain matters: TeraWulf's 'Fluidstack' leases were widely mapped to Anthropic as end user months before Anthropic signed a direct 20-year, 401 MW lease and made it explicit
Direct-lab leases beat middleman leases on credit quality; the trade-off is fewer, bigger counterparties — concentration risk in a different costume

A 'net generator' campus flips the grid relationship: build your own on-site generation plus batteries, sell surplus back — the utility becomes the customer, and the interconnection queue stops being the constraint

sections.heading: Zero-carbon claims: how to evaluate them
bullets: 'Powered by ~90% zero-carbon energy' usually means the regional grid mix (upstate NY runs heavily on hydro and nuclear), not that the facility bought dedicated clean supply

The strict standard requires RECs (renewable energy certificates) or a direct PPA with a specific generator; grid-mix claims without them draw greenwashing critiques — TeraWulf took exactly this fire from short-sellers in 2024
Siting in a clean-grid zone is still economically real: power there is often cheap AND clean (hydro), and tenants' ESG reporting benefits from location-based accounting
Watch the definitions in any 'zero-carbon' marketing: location-based (grid mix) vs market-based (certificates purchased) accounting can tell opposite stories about the same building

flashcards.q: Why is a dead coal plant or smelter worth hundreds of millions to a data-center developer?
flashcards.a: The energized substation and high-voltage interconnect. New grid connections queue for years; a brownfield inherits one that already carried hundreds of megawatts — the buyer is paying for the wire, not the land.

flashcards.q: What's the difference between gross MW and critical IT MW?
flashcards.a: Gross is total site draw from the grid; critical IT is what reaches the computers. The ratio between them is PUE — a 1.25 PUE site needs 125 MW gross to deliver 100 MW of IT load.

flashcards.q: Why can't a bitcoin-mining hall just be handed to an AI tenant?
flashcards.a: Mining runs cheap air-cooled racks (~30 kW) with no redundancy. AI hosting needs direct-to-chip liquid cooling at 130+ kW per rack, backup power, and concurrent maintainability — it's a rebuild on the same power, roughly $9-12M per critical-IT MW.

flashcards.q: What is a lease backstop and what does the backstopper get?
flashcards.a: A guarantee by a strong balance sheet to cover (up to a cap) a weak tenant's lease payments if it defaults, making the lease bankable. The backstopper is typically paid in penny warrants — equity upside as the insurance premium.

flashcards.q: Why do backstopped leases enable construction debt?
flashcards.a: Lenders fund against contracted cash flows. A thin-credit tenant's promise isn't lendable; the same promise wrapped in an investment-grade guarantee is — so a subsidiary can issue notes secured by the lease and build the building.

flashcards.q: A landlord's stock doubles and it reports a $750M quarterly loss. What probably happened?
flashcards.a: Warrant mark-to-market. Outstanding warrants are a liability re-measured each quarter; when the stock rises the liability grows and the company books a non-cash loss. GAAP earnings become anti-correlated with success.

flashcards.q: What metrics actually track an AI landlord's health, if not EPS?
flashcards.a: Contracted MW and its energization schedule vs plan, build cost per critical-IT MW vs guidance, NOI margin per lease, and cash vs remaining capex. Backlog converts to revenue only when buildings energize.

flashcards.q: What is take-or-pay and why does it define this sector?
flashcards.a: The tenant owes rent whether or not it uses the capacity. It turns a lease into a bond-like cash stream — the foundation under every backstop, project note, and backlog number in AI hosting.

flashcards.q: Why does the tenant chain (lab → cloud middleman → landlord) matter?
flashcards.a: Credit lives at the ends of the chain. A middleman's lease is only as good as who stands behind it — following the chain reveals the real counterparty and the real risk, and direct-lab leases remove a layer entirely.

flashcards.q: What is a 'net generator' or BYOG campus?
flashcards.a: Bring Your Own Generation: on-site power plants plus batteries sized beyond the data-center load, selling surplus to the grid. It sidesteps the interconnection queue and turns the utility relationship from constraint into revenue.

flashcards.q: When is a '90% zero-carbon' claim solid vs greenwash?
flashcards.a: Solid if backed by RECs or a direct PPA with a clean generator (market-based accounting). If it just cites the regional grid mix (location-based), the facility is riding hydro/nuclear averages it didn't contract for — cheap and cleaner, but not certified clean.

flashcards.q: Why do long-lead electrical components set AI buildout schedules?
flashcards.a: Transformers, switchgear, and chillers run multi-year order books industry-wide. GPU racks arrive in months; the electrical gear feeding them is the bottleneck, so delivery promises live or die on procurement done years ahead.
